Both Aminolevulinic Acid and Ingenol Mebutate are known to induce Keratoacanthoma, a skin lesion characterized by the proliferation of keratinocytes. The shared association of Diclofenac with these conditions implies a possible mechanism by which Diclofenac may contribute to the development of Keratoacanthoma, though the exact nature of this relationship remains unclear. The evidence highlights a potential pathway where Diclofenac could influence the progression of Inverted Follicular Keratosis, which in turn may lead to Keratoacanthoma, though further research is needed to confirm this mechanism.
